title: A work item's timeline: stage, holder, lease, history, links and thread in one read

story.as_a: Mark in fleet_dash, or a session about to take an item over
story.i_want_to: read one work item's whole state and history in one call
story.so_that: I can see where it is, who holds it, why it moved and what is linked to it without reconstructing it from five reads

rationale: PRD R4 asks for 'visibility into each part of the process' through an API and MCP built on the event log. Today the facts are scattered: GET /stories/:id/stage (story_escalation_controller.ex:223) returns the stage row only, GET /stories/:id/history (story_history_controller.ex:50) returns audit_log rows with no MCP tool (route_coverage.test.js:234 lists it as a gap), and the holder, lease, issue, PR, CI runs and thread are each in another table. This story builds the per-item read on release 3's event log and replaces the history route, which it subsumes.

acceptance_criteria.description: Loopctl.Delivery.Timeline.events/3 (tenant_id, story_id, opts) returns the item's story_stage_events rows and its audit_log rows (entity_type 'story', entity_id story_id) merged oldest first, each as %{source: :stage_event | :audit, event, from, to, edge, actor_label, actor_holder_id, reason, at}, keyset-paginated on (at, source, id) with limit default 100 and max 500 and a next cursor.

Timeline.current/2 returns stage, stage_entered_at (inserted_at of the newest 'transitioned' event whose to_stage is the current stage, else the 'opened' event) and age_seconds measured from it; a story with no stage row returns stage nil and age_seconds nil.

Timeline.current/2 returns holder %{holder_id, kind, host, worktree, session_id, last_seen_at} read from the holders row named by stories.assigned_holder_id, and lease %{claim_epoch, claimed_until}; an unclaimed item returns holder nil with its claim_epoch.

Timeline.current/2 returns links: the intake record's repo_full_name, issue_number, html_url and generation (nil without one), the stage row's pr_number, branch and head_sha, the runner %{id, name} named by story_stages.runner_id, and ci_runs: the story's verification_runs rows (status, commit_sha, logs_url, completed_at), newest first, at most 20.

Timeline.current/2 returns thread %{count, messages}: the count of the item's thread messages (release 4 message rows attached by story_id) and the newest 20, read without creating or advancing any channel_cursors row.

GET /api/v1/stories/:id/timeline (role: :agent, so a holder credential, an orchestrator key and fleet_dash's user key all pass) answers %{item: current, events: page, next_cursor}; every reason and message body carries untrusted: true; an unknown story or another tenant's story is 404.

MCP tool work_item_timeline calls the route with story_id, cursor and limit, has a row in mcp-server/README.md, and is pinned by a declared-and-dispatched wiring test; its description says the reasons are untrusted session text.
GET /api/v1/stories/:id/history, LoopctlWeb.StoryHistoryController and its route_coverage gap row are deleted; the timeline's :audit events carry every entry the history route returned.

The end-to-end scenario two_sessions_one_repo (US-52.20) gains a step that reads each item's work_item_timeline and asserts a claimed event by the item's own holder with a non-empty reason, and no event of either item naming the other session's holder.

test_cases.name: events merge stage events and audit rows in order and page by cursor (DataCase)
preconditions: tenant = fixture(:tenant); story = fixture(:story, tenant_id: tenant.id); Stages.open/3 then three advances; two Audit entries for the story between them
expected_results: 6 rows over two pages in timestamp order, no row twice

test_cases.name: stage age counts from the transition into the current stage (DataCase)
preconditions: a story advanced detected -> triaged -> queued with known inserted_at values; a story with no stage row
expected_results: current(story) returns stage queued, stage_entered_at equal to the inserted_at of the 'transitioned' event whose to_stage is queued, and age_seconds measured from that time
current(bare) returns stage nil and age_seconds nil

test_cases.name: holder and lease come from the claim's holder (DataCase)
preconditions: a holders row (release 3 fixture) assigned to a claimed story with claimed_until set; a second, unclaimed story
expected_results: the claimed story returns holder %{holder_id, kind, host, worktree, session_id, last_seen_at} read from the holders row named by assigned_holder_id, and lease %{claim_epoch, claimed_until}
the unclaimed story returns holder nil with its claim_epoch

test_cases.name: links name the issue, PR, runner and CI runs (DataCase)
preconditions: an intake record linked to the story; stage row with pr_number, branch, head_sha, runner_id of fixture(:runner); 22 verification_runs rows

test_cases.name: the thread is read without touching a cursor (DataCase)
preconditions: 25 thread messages on the item (release 4 fixture); a holder with a channel_cursors row for the thread

test_cases.name: route roles, untrusted flags and tenant isolation (ConnCase)
preconditions: a holder agent key, an orchestrator key and a user key in tenant A; a story in tenant B
steps: GET tenant B's story with tenant A's key
expected_results: 200 for all three keys; 404 for tenant B's story

test_cases.name: work_item_timeline wiring and request shape (node --test)
preconditions: mcp-server tool list and a stub apiCall

test_cases.name: the history route is gone and its entries are in the timeline (ConnCase)
expected_results: 404 for history; every audit entry appears once as an :audit event

test_cases.name: two_sessions_one_repo reads its event log through the timeline (e2e)
preconditions: mix e2e against loopctl.com after this release deploys
expected_results: each item's timeline shows a claimed event by its own holder with a non-empty reason
no event of either item names the other session's holder

technical_notes: Stage events: Loopctl.Delivery.StageEvent (lib/loopctl/delivery/stage_event.ex:40-51), read today by Stages.list_events/2 (lib/loopctl/delivery/stages.ex:451); actor_holder_id and the required reason on every event are provided by release 3 (README names table: work-item event log). Index story_stage_events (tenant_id, story_id, inserted_at) exists (priv/repo/migrations/20260915120000_create_story_stages.exs:113).

Audit rows: the query StoryHistoryController.query_history/3 runs (lib/loopctl_web/controllers/story_history_controller.ex:74) moves into Timeline; delete the controller, its route (lib/loopctl_web/router.ex:447) and the gap row (mcp-server/test/route_coverage.test.js:234).

Docs: CLAUDE.md's Epic 17 'Audit API' bullet (CLAUDE.md:725-726) and docs/orchestration-guide.md:163-181 describe GET /stories/:id/history as live; both are rewritten in the same commit to point at work_item_timeline.

Why a new route rather than extending GET /stories/:id/stage: that route is the stage row the runner and story_stage read (story_escalation_controller.ex:367 render_stage/1); its shape is a contract, and a paginated history does not belong in it. The stage route stays.

Holder: holders table and stories.assigned_holder_id are provided by release 3 (README names table: holder, the claim's holder). Lease: stories.claim_epoch and claimed_until (lib/loopctl/work_breakdown/story.ex:130-131).

Links: stories.intake_record_id (story.ex:121) -> Loopctl.Intake.Record (lib/loopctl/intake/record.ex:63-67); story_stages pr_number/branch/head_sha/runner_id (lib/loopctl/delivery/story_stage.ex:64-69); runners.name (lib/loopctl/runners/runner.ex:93); verification_runs (lib/loopctl/verification/verification_run.ex:32-43).

Thread: release 4's message row (README names table: message, story_id attachment) and channel_cursors; this read never writes a cursor, so fleet_dash reading an item does not mark anything read for its holder.
Reads run on Repo inside Repo.with_tenant/2 with an explicit tenant_id predicate on every table (the EscalationInbox.list/2 convention, lib/loopctl/delivery/escalation_inbox.ex:237).

MCP: add lib/work-item.js with the request shape, a declaration and a case in mcp-server/index.js beside story_stage (~:8971), a README row, and a test like mcp-server/test/delivery_loop_tools.test.js.
non_goals: Any write, including marking the thread read: release 4's inbox owns cursors.

failure_modes.partition: n/a: a read inside one request against loopctl's own Postgres; no second service is called (CI runs come from verification_runs rows, never from the forge).
failure_modes.state: AC-52.29.1: the history is the event log and the audit log, both append-only in Postgres; the timeline holds nothing of its own, so a restart loses nothing.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.29.5: the read writes nothing, the thread cursor included, so a repeated call changes no state.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.29.1: the page is bounded (max 500 events) and keyset-paginated on an indexed column, so a long-lived item never produces an unbounded response; AC-52.29.4 caps ci_runs at 20.
failure_modes.reach: n/a: runs inline in the request process; nothing is queued.

definition_of_done: From an MCP session on production, work_item_timeline for a delivered story returns its holder, its PR and every transition with an actor and a reason.
curl of GET /api/v1/stories/<id>/history on the deployed app returns 404.
defaults: Page size: 100 events, at most 500 (owner may change).
ci_runs and thread messages: the newest 20 each (owner may change).
Who may read: every role from :agent up, like every other read on this surface.
